section:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate ONE exceptionally polished desktop website section design for 8x Social, 1536x1024 landscape composition. This is the section AFTER a carbon-black hero and creator video examples. It should feel like the same continuous editorial page. Quiet confident Silicon Valley brand, disciplined Swiss type, not a generic SaaS dashboard.
Image 1 is the USER'S EDGE-TREATMENT REFERENCE ONLY: use its fine raster-dot image perimeter. Do NOT reuse its five studio faces. Image 2 is the actual current creator-content website design: keep its typography spirit, proportions and brand palette. Image 3 is the REAL ORIGINAL creator poster to use in the new media area, not a face to invent.
Palette ONLY warm stone #E9E5DC for this section, carbon #111111 for text, signal orange #F34B32 for one active accent. Authentic photographic content can retain subdued natural color. No white cards, no blue/purple, no shiny effects.
Composition: full flat warm-stone surface, generous 75px side margins, clean 2-column editorial layout. At top show a 90px sliver of outgoing charcoal page; a very narrow 28px field of tiny charcoal raster dots becomes sparse as it meets stone. This is a page boundary, not a particle explosion or curved wipe. Below give 100px breathing space.
Left roughly 50%: boldly typeset heading EXACT 'Your network.' newline 'Our day-to-day.' in black, 65px modern grotesk, tight tracking, no eyebrow or chapter number. Body below at24px EXACT 'From finding creators to keeping content moving.' Beneath it a generous 45px gap then three thin ruled accordion rows, no boxes/cards:
'Find your people.' orange small solid circular active marker at far right, below this row's title show EXACT 'Creators who fit your category and audience.'
'Keep content moving.' simple small plus at far right.
'See what works.' simple small plus at far right.
Active row's rule has a short orange segment. At bottom a simple text CTA 'Build your network' and diagonal arrow, no pill.
Right roughly 42%: one tall elegant portrait-format creator film window, about360pxwide x540high, vertically aligned with headline. Use the actual Judy poster (image3) with full head and shoulders and laptop, never studio portraits. Remove subtitle text ONLY in the conceptual representation if needed. Natural subdued photo, not fake chart or new UI. The rectangle's LEFT AND RIGHT edges dissolve through a restrained 14–22px band of tiny fine evenly spaced raster dots into stone, exactly the spirit of the user's reference. Center photo remains sharp, not halftone. No frame, no shadow, no bevel, no rounded-card border. Under it one low-key attribution '@judyintech' and a small media play symbol. Tiny dots, not coarse dot field; no floating particles elsewhere. Asymmetric balance, purposeful negative space, refined line lengths and typesetting. Do not include a second navbar or giant logo in this section. No fake metrics, stars, trust badges, dashboards, glass, 3D, clouds, ribbons, repeated hero portrait montage or decorative captions. Output only a beautiful realistic website section screenshot, not a moodboard or device mockup.
transition:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create an exceptionally clean 4-frame animation storyboard for the 8x Social website, landscape 2048x1536, a precise 2x2 grid. It explains ONE continuous document scrolling from existing charcoal creator content into the new stone management section. Not four different page redesigns. Reference1 is the approved-to-review NEW stone-section concept; reference2 is the EXISTING black creator-content section. Preserve their actual layouts and the original creator media faithfully. Use black#111111, warm stone#E9E5DC, orange#F34B32 only for UI. No studio hero faces.
Each viewport frame same aspect ratio and same width; calm gutters; clear labels ABOVE frames, outside website UI. Board header 'One page. A quieter hand-off.' secondary small 'Scroll moves the page. Dots stay at the edges.'
FRAME01 label '01 / LEAVE THE WORK': the existing charcoal content section with its left headline 'Creator content. Built for the feed.' and three right creator clips remains recognizably intact; the stone next section is just beginning to appear at bottom70px through a narrow 24px fine equal-dot printed boundary. No full-page tint, no horizontal morph.
FRAME02 label '02 / CROSS THE SEAM': same document after ordinary downward scroll. Lower portion of existing black section occupies top35percent, stone occupies bottom65percent. The same fine dot seam sits at the color boundary. New 'Your network. Our day-to-day.' heading and original Judy media area enter naturally from below. Previous content moves up without shrinking, dissolving, reordering or flying. Only a narrow 10–20px dot rim along new photograph's side edges animates into place.
FRAME03 label '03 / SETTLE ON STONE': new stone section fully visible matching reference1: headline left, one original Judy video at right with fine raster-dot side edges, thin three accordion rows 'Find your people.', 'Keep content moving.', 'See what works.' First row expanded with 'Creators who fit your category and audience.' Orange dot and short orange rule mark active row. Same dimensions and alignment as final reference. Faces remain clear. No new header or repeated giantlogo.
FRAME04 label '04 / CHANGE ONLY THE DETAIL': IDENTICAL stone viewport geometry to frame03. Headline, stone background, outer media rectangle fixed exactly. Second accordion row active, small orange dot moves to this row and the corresponding short rule becomes orange; description 'Briefs, reviews and publishing. Kept moving by 8x.' The media shows another moment from the SAME Judy clip, or the original source Jack video if absolutely needed, with no enlarging or shifting frame. A tiny local fine-dot ripple runs only along the photo edge, subtly indicated using a small unobtrusive arrow outside the image edge in the board gutter; no arrows over faces. No orange takeover, no map in this storyboard.
Below frames a small concise notation '24px seam • 14px photo rim • 240ms local changes • native scroll'. This is design annotation outside the website, not permanent webpage text. Make the board visually gorgeous, legible, disciplined. No gradients flooding viewport, particle clouds, disconnected cards, fake UI, 3D, diagram nodes, decorative badges, inventedmetrics or repeated hero portraits. Motion should look subtle, local and executable, not a cinema sequence. Prioritize exact consistency between frames03and04.
